takeaways: Vistra's Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA jumped more than 50% to $2.378 billion, helped by higher realized energy and capacity prices, Lotus-acquired plants, and Martin Lake Unit 1 back online after a hot summer of record demand in ERCOT and PJM.

Revenue of $6.347 billion rose 28% year over year but missed Investing.com's $6.79 billion consensus; GAAP net income still climbed to $1.14 billion from $652 million, including a $559 million unrealized hedge gain expected to settle in future years.
Management raised and narrowed 2026 Ongoing Ops Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $7.1–$7.5 billion and initiated 2027 guidance of $7.7–$8.5 billion.

The board authorized another $1.5 billion of buybacks (about $2.5 billion total authorization left, aimed by year-end 2028), and Vistra closed the Cogentrix deal adding roughly 5,500 MW of gas generation in October.
Investing.com notes shares rose about 5% premarket even with the revenue miss — the EBITDA print and guide mattered more to traders.
verdict: Miss the top line, crush the cash engine, raise the guide, add buybacks — classic Vistra. A blistering summer and higher power prices did the heavy lifting, and Wall Street cheered the EBITDA anyway. Max's take: when your product is electrons in a heat wave, the income statement kind of writes itself.

sources.title: Investing.com: Vistra stock jumps despite revenue miss
